spec_match.rationale: Covers the direction-sensitivity angle properly: LTR right-edge vs RTL left-edge ellipsis across Arabic, Hebrew and Persian samples, a genuinely bidirectional Arabic-with-Latin-runs field, plus full-width LTR/RTL URL bars — exactly the writing-direction claim the feature makes.

interactive.rationale: Seven focusable fields with live badges, a width slider and font-size toggle that re-style the inputs, and two full-width URL bars — a genuine tester, not a code-card (assessed from code review and the rendered DOM).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card's promise (direction grid, RTL scripts, width slider, font toggle, full-width URL bars) matches the page; the new bidi field strengthens the 'bidirectional text' claim in the lede.

edge_cases.rationale: RTL scripts, a mixed-direction bidi field and width/font permutations are real edge coverage; vertical writing modes and non-input ellipsis contexts remain unexplored.

conformance.rationale: The shared feature suite runs 9 pass / 0 fail here, but it checks prerequisites only and has no direction-aware or focused-state assertion, so it cannot fail on a pre-149 browser. Existing suite is immutable; noted, not changed.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Cloud-fallback observation, NOT chrome-devtools-mcp browser verification (auto-research.md §0 blocker applies): headless Chromium 141 full-page screenshots at 1280px, DOM dump confirming all 7 aria-labels, aria-pressed true/false pair and the honest focus readout strings, plus `deno task responsive-check v149/clip-text-overflow-on-user-interaction --merge` passing desktop and mobile with no horizontal overflow and clean console/network. Focus transitions, slider and toggle were not driven interactively; that remains for an MCP-equipped session.

telemetry_health.rationale: Only the server-injected baseline telemetry is present; no custom interaction/assert events for the direction tests.

design_system.rationale: All colours are design-system variables after the 2026-10-18 fix (.test-input:focus now uses var(--bg-ivory)); .toggle-btn.active sets background and color together.

accessibility.rationale: Fixed 2026-10-18: every generated input now carries aria-label '<card title> test field' (7/7 verified in the served DOM), the Normal/Large toggle exposes aria-pressed and updates it on click, and :focus-visible outlines were added for test inputs, wide inputs and toggle buttons. Remaining gap: the focused/blurred badges and overflow-viz readouts are still not live regions, so state changes are visual-only for screen readers.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: deno task responsive-check (mobile ≈360×740 DPR3 touch + desktop 1280×800) passes both classes with no horizontal overflow and clean console/network; the checker notes sub-44px tap targets on the small state badges (advisory, non-interactive elements).

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible names and focus indicators for dynamically generated form inputs
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Give every control a programmatic name and a visible focus indicator; keep toggle state programmatic (aria-pressed).
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: applied: aria-label derived from each card title on every generated input, aria-pressed on the font-size toggle kept in sync on click, :focus-visible outline (2px accent, offset) added instead of the removed default outline
guidanceConsulted.evidence: DOM dump shows 7 aria-labels and aria-pressed true/false; responsive-check passes both classes

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible names and focus indicators for dynamically generated form inputs
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Form fields need labels or equivalent accessible names; do not rely on adjacent visual text.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: applied: card titles are now attached to their inputs via aria-label rather than being unassociated visual text

openQuestions.title: Announce focus-state changes to screen readers
openQuestions.detail: The focused/blurred badge and the overflow-viz readout update visually on focus/blur but are not aria-live regions, so non-visual users get no equivalent of the state change. Add a polite live region (or aria-live on the badge) — taking care not to spam announcements while tabbing through all seven fields.

openQuestions.title: Verify the clip-on-focus behavior interactively on Chrome 149+
openQuestions.detail: The focus readout is now honestly labelled 'Chrome 149+ clips … — manual observation', but no session has yet driven focus/blur on a 149+ browser via chrome-devtools-mcp and visually confirmed the ellipsis disappears per direction. Do that once an MCP-equipped session with Chrome 149+ is available.

openQuestions.title: Add a scrollWidth/scrollLeft measurement probe
openQuestions.detail: A measured observable (comparing scrollLeft reachability or selection scroll before/after focus) could turn the manual-observation readout into a real probe that can return false on pre-149 browsers. Worth exploring, but the measurement is subtle (focus scrolls the caret) — prototype carefully before shipping.

summary: Weekly hardening pass 2026-10-18 (headless Chromium 141 cloud fallback, not chrome-devtools-mcp): fixed the major accessibility question — all seven generated inputs now have accessible names (verified 7/7 in the served DOM), the font-size toggle exposes synced aria-pressed, and :focus-visible outlines replace the removed default outline. Also fixed: focused input background now var(--bg-ivory) (design-system minor), the focus readout is honestly labelled as a Chrome 149+ manual observation instead of an unconditional 'clipped' claim (moderate), and an additive bidi field (Arabic base with Latin runs) covers the promised bidirectional case (minor). deno task responsive-check passes desktop and mobile with no horizontal overflow and clean console/network. Remaining: live-region announcements and a true measured probe.
